principles.name: Select an opaque door patch and preserve the cavity relationship
principles.applicability: Closing a hinged panel when a camera view shows both the microwave cavity and the door attachment edge.
observable_failure_signals: The selected region's fitted normal points vertically despite the door being upright.
The surface fit has a large residual or the preview overlay falls in the window opening.
A push disturbs nearby tabletop objects while the cavity-door alignment does not improve.
conditional_actions: Choose a smaller patch on the opaque frame or solid door surface, away from the transparent opening.
Use a larger target region on the same visible door to assess the door-cavity relationship.
Preview the new geometry and inspect the measured point, normal, and overlay before acting.
principles.limits: Supported by six attempts in one scene. A visually plausible patch can still select background through a window; a horizontal normal alone does not prove that a region belongs to the door. A solid patch also may fail when the current door orientation makes the approach or direction unsuitable.

principles.name: Choose push direction from the current door orientation
principles.applicability: A door remains visibly open after a physical push and its face or edge orientation has changed.
observable_failure_signals: The door swings farther away from covering the cavity after a push.
The robot reaches the selected surface but native task success remains false.
Repeated same-direction actions produce no closing relationship or continue the wrong swing.
conditional_actions: Reobserve the current panel and cavity from a view that exposes the attachment edge.
Estimate the current face normal again and select the inward push direction relative to the cavity.
If the observed panel moves away from closure, change the direction for the next bounded physical experiment instead of repeating the old sign.
Use the native task result and image relationship after every executed push; motion-tracker failure alone is inconclusive.
principles.limits: Successful actions used different observed faces and directions. Attempts 3, 4, 5, and 6 each needed direction or contact changes after an unsuccessful motion. These outcomes do not provide a universal world direction or prove the same rule for other hinges.

principles.name: Treat motion-tracker failure as unresolved motion
principles.applicability: A contact skill returns without task success and reports too few RGB-D feature correspondences.
observable_failure_signals: The tracker reports insufficient visible matches.
The action executed, but the returned measurement is not accepted.
conditional_actions: Compare fresh images of the door, cavity, and nearby objects to judge actual direction and progress.
If the door relationship improved, select fresh geometry and continue toward closure.
If it worsened or stayed open, change the contact region or direction based on the current view.
Keep native task success as the completion test.
principles.limits: The tracker was unresolved on multiple physical pushes, including some followed by visible scene changes. Image interpretation is qualitative and can be obscured by the robot; it does not substitute for a native success result.

principles.name: Replan on the current solid side frame after the door swings
principles.applicability: A bounded action changes the door angle but leaves the cavity visibly uncovered, exposing a new opaque side or edge of the door.
observable_failure_signals: The task remains incomplete after a push and the door has visibly changed angle.
The current contact preview lands in the window opening or fits the tabletop.
A push along an estimated door-to-cavity vector moves the door but does not reduce the visible opening.
conditional_actions: Capture a fresh view and select a solid side border on the door's current orientation.
Check that the selected surface normal is consistent with the visible upright panel and that the overlay covers the door frame.
Use a new bounded push directed into the current face, then judge the updated door-cavity relationship and native task result.
If the door moves away from closure, change direction based on the new view rather than reusing the prior world vector.
principles.limits: Attempts 4 and 5 succeeded from a changed door orientation after earlier actions; attempt 6 succeeded after one unsuccessful initial side-frame push. This supports fresh replanning after motion, not a one-push reset method or a general hinge rule.
